messages.subject: agrad::var as smart pointer
parts:
These C++ design books are enlightening.

It turns out that our stan::agrad::var class is an
instance of what's known as a "smart pointer". That
is, it holds onto a pointer, has value (copy) semantics,
and manages its pointer resources internally.

I added two functions that are conventional for
smart pointers, operator*() and operator->(), so
that the following test now passes:

typedef stan::agrad::var AVAR;

TEST(AgradAgrad, smart_ptrs) {
AVAR a = 2.0;
EXPECT_FLOAT_EQ(2.0, (*a).val_); // operator*
EXPECT_FLOAT_EQ(2.0, a->val_); // operator->

EXPECT_FLOAT_EQ(2.0,(*a.vi_).val_);
EXPECT_FLOAT_EQ(2.0,a.vi_->val_);
}

As you can see, operator*() returns
the same as *(a.vi_) and a-> acts
like a.vi_->.

This'll simplify all the vari definitions.

- Bob
